描述_ZN: The Poem of the Yuan People" scroll, Qing dynasty, inscribed by Liang Shi, on paper in running script, 129 cm long and 56.8 cm wide.　　Commentary: Every time I remember the road to the west of the city, I used to come to the Pavilion of Good Paintings. The orchids are white through the rain, and the wild bamboos are green into the clouds.　　The waves and shadows float in the spring, and the mountains are lit up by daytime Bibimbap. The moon shines in the coolness of the moon.　　The Yuan Dynasty. Liang Shizheng.　　Signed "Liang Shizheng", with a white seal of "Liang Shizheng" and a vermilion seal of "Xianglin". At the beginning of the quotation, it is inscribed with the oval seal in vermilion, "Seal of the Servant in front of the Twelfth Floor".　　This painting is one of "Five Poems on the Pavilion of Playfulness" written by Wang Shixi of Yuan Dynasty. Liang Shizheng learned calligraphy from Liu Gongquan at the beginning, and later he studied with Zhao Mengfu and Wen Zhengming, and in his later years he studied with Yan Zhenqing and Li Yong. The strokes of this work are stretched, the characters are tightly knitted, and the bones are strong and robust, gathering the strength of many schools and achieving a graceful and handsome appearance.
